patient.name: Bernard Okwuosa
patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral leg weakness and numbness worsening over 4 months, cannot climb stairs
patient.hpi: Bernard Okwuosa is a 62-year-old retired high school principal with a 4-month history of progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness and numbness that has not responded to pregabalin initiated by his primary care physician. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 8 years ago, and his primary care physician attributed his current symptoms to diabetic peripheral neuropathy. However, his neurologist notes several features atypical for diabetic neuropathy: the weakness is prominent and proximal as well as distal, the course has been rapidly progressive over only 4 months rather than the gradual years-long progression of diabetic neuropathy, and his right upper extremity has recently become involved with hand weakness and difficulty opening jars. He reports bilateral foot and calf numbness and tingling beginning 4 months ago, followed within 6 weeks by prominent thigh weakness making stair-climbing difficult. He struggles to rise from low chairs and has fallen twice. He reports new right hand weakness over the past 6 weeks. He denies bowel or bladder involvement. His HbA1c has been 7.2% for the past year on metformin and sitagliptin. He has no history of alcohol use, recent travel, or toxic exposures. He denies weight loss. A prior NCS performed by his primary care physician 3 years ago showed mild axonal changes attributed to diabetes. He is now referred to neurology for progressive weakness not fitting diabetic neuropathy.

output.impression: This is a NORMAL EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no electrographic seizures recorded. Awake background alpha rhythm at 10 Hz bilaterally, symmetric and reactive. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: Right peroneal motor velocity 38.2 m/s (L), Right tibial motor velocity 36.8 m/s (L), Right peroneal conduction block 33% amplitude drop (H), Right sural SNAP amplitude 4.2 uV (L). Mixed demyelinating and axonal features with conduction block at a non-compressive site. EMG shows active denervation with polyphasic motor unit potentials in proximal lower extremity musculature.

Markedly elevated CSF protein at 118 mg/dL with normal cell count (2 WBC/uL) — a pattern of albumino-cytologic dissociation. No pleocytosis. No malignant cells on cytology. No oligoclonal bands. Clinical correlation recommended.
All values within normal limits. IgA 284 mg/dL (normal range). Anti-NF155 and anti-CNTN1 negative. No M-spike on repeat SPEP.

output.tracer_or_protocol: T1 post-contrast, T2, STIR sequences; gadolinium 0.1 mmol/kg

findings.description: Cervical spine: Mild C5-C6 neural foraminal narrowing without cord compression or cord signal abnormality. Lumbar spine: Mild L4-L5 and L5-S1 disc bulging without significant canal stenosis. No epidural collection. Nerve roots: Bilateral posterior nerve root enhancement at L4-S1 on gadolinium-enhanced sequences; mildly thickened, clumped cauda equina nerve roots with gadolinium enhancement bilaterally. Conus medullaris: normal signal.

output.impression: 1. Bilateral gadolinium enhancement of posterior nerve roots at L4-S1 with mildly thickened, clumped cauda equina nerve roots — an inflammatory/infiltrative polyradiculopathy is favored; neoplastic infiltration is less likely but not excluded. 2. Mild C5-C6 neural foraminal narrowing without cord compression. 3. Mild L4-L5 and L5-S1 disc bulging without significant canal stenosis. 4. Normal conus medullaris signal. No epidural abscess. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Segmental demyelination and remyelination with onion bulb formations (concentric Schwann cell processes wrapping single axons — hallmark of repeated demyelination)
Moderate endoneurial fibrosis. Patchy mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate (CD8+ T cells and macrophages) in endoneurium and perineurium.
Vasculitis: ABSENT — no epineurial or endoneurial vasculitis.
Congo red: Negative for amyloid. No IgG/IgA/IgM/complement deposits on myelin.
Electron microscopy: Onion bulbs confirmed; widely-spaced myelin lamellae absent.

output.impression: Sural nerve biopsy shows segmental demyelination and remyelination with onion bulb formations and macrophage-associated demyelination. Patchy endoneurial T-cell and macrophage infiltrate. Moderate axonal loss. No vasculitis. Congo red negative for amyloid. Widely-spaced myelin lamellae absent on electron microscopy. Findings indicate a demyelinating neuropathy with active inflammatory features; clinical and electrodiagnostic correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Repeat electrophysiology recommended to monitor interval change.

output.query: CIDP superimposed on diabetic neuropathy diagnosis treatment IVIG

results.citation: Laughlin RS et al. (2009) CIDP in diabetes. Neurology 73:697-701.
results.summary: CIDP occurs 11x more frequently in diabetic patients. Distinguishing features from diabetic neuropathy: proximal weakness, rapid progression, CSF protein >80 mg/dL, demyelinating NCS with conduction block. IVIG response rate 70-80% in CIDP with diabetes.

results.citation: Vallat JM et al. (2010) Nerve biopsy in CIDP. J Neurol 257:1386-1389.
results.summary: Onion bulb formations on sural nerve biopsy confirm CIDP when NCS criteria are borderline. Anti-NF155/CNTN1 positive nodopathy variants are IVIG-refractory — test before initiating IVIG.

output.summary: IVIG, corticosteroids, and plasma exchange are established immunomodulatory treatments for CIDP with class I–II evidence. Randomized trials show approximately 70–80% short-term response rate to IVIG in CIDP. CIDP occurs at higher frequency in patients with diabetes mellitus, and electrodiagnostic criteria for CIDP in this population require attention to conduction block at non-compressive sites. IgA measurement before IVIG administration is standard practice. Nodal/paranodal antibody status (anti-NF155, anti-CNTN1) may predict differential treatment response.

output.proposed: IVIG 2g/kg induction + Metformin 1000 mg twice daily + Atorvastatin 40 mg daily + Lisinopril 10 mg daily
interactions: drugs: ["IVIG", "Metformin"]; severity: minor; description: IVIG may cause transient glucose fluctuations due to sucrose or glucose stabilizers in some formulations. Monitor blood glucose during and 24-48 hours after IVIG infusion. Use sucrose-free IVIG formulations (Gammagard Liquid, Privigen) in diabetic patients.
warnings: Use sucrose-free IVIG formulation for this diabetic patient. Monitor glucose during infusion.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) superimposed on diabetic axonal polyneuropathy

differential.key_features: Real contributor (axonal layer); does not explain demyelinating features or rapid 4-month progression.
Uniformly slow velocities without conduction block; need family history, pes cavus, genetic panel.
Pure motor with conduction block; sensory involvement here excludes MMN.
Lambda monoclonal protein + organomegaly + endocrinopathy + elevated VEGF; need SPEP/VEGF/skeletal survey.
Asymmetric multifocal axonal; CIDP is symmetric demyelinating.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture for CSF when CIDP suspected
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein, normal cell count) supports CIDP

optimal_actions.action: Pre-IVIG safety screen (IgA, IgG subclasses, anti-NF155/CNTN1 nodal antibodies)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal IgA (rules out anaphylaxis risk); negative nodal antibodies (anti-NF155+ CIDP responds poorly to IVIG)

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.
Document coagulation and platelet status before lumbar puncture.

critical_actions: Recognize rapid 4-month progression with proximal involvement as atypical for distal diabetic neuropathy
Lumbar puncture for albuminocytologic dissociation supporting CIDP
Initiate IVIG 2 g/kg induction (first-line for CIDP)
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute everything to diabetes — demyelinating velocities and proximal weakness require CIDP workup
Do not start IVIG without checking IgA
key_reasoning_points: CIDP superimposed on diabetic neuropathy is well-described; CIDP is treatable, do not miss it
Demyelinating velocities + CSF albuminocytologic dissociation + response to immunotherapy = CIDP
Anti-NF155+ nodopathies are IVIG-refractory and respond to rituximab

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on diabetic neuropathy and miss CIDP
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Diabetes is a contributor but cannot explain rapid 4-month progression with proximal weakness and demyelinating NCS pattern.
